text:
In 1997 about two-thirds of the world’s population, roughly 3.7–3.9 billion of about 5.85 billion people, lived in countries with per capita income of $1230 or less. That group included China (about $860) and India (about $400), along with Indonesia and most of South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. China reached upper-middle income only around 2010, and India was still low-income in 1997.

CONFIDENCE: 70
